claims.statement: The pytest unit suite runs in asyncio auto mode (asyncio_mode = "auto"), so async test functions and fixtures are awaited without any per-test asyncio marker.
Pytest collection is rooted at the tests/ directory via testpaths = ["tests"], so a bare pytest run discovers the entire unit suite there.
Test tooling (pytest, pytest-asyncio, ruff, basedpyright, Pygments) is declared in the dev optional-dependency group and installed via `make install` which runs `uv sync --extra dev`.

tests/conftest.py provides a fake_store fixture that routes every agent.store access to an in-memory FakeStore, which round-trips values through the real agent.store code path (model_dump/model_validate) the way production does.
An autouse _reset_ttl_cache fixture clears the process-global TTL cache before and after each test so cached team settings do not leak between tests.

An autouse _default_enable_auto_review fixture stubs is_review_repo_enabled to return True for every repo, because the dashboard opt-in list is empty without a live Store; tests targeting the auto-review gate must override it with a stricter stub.

Unit tests are run with `make test` (aliased `make tests`), which executes `uv run pytest -vvv $(TEST_FILE)` where TEST_FILE defaults to tests/ and a single file or single test can be targeted by overriding TEST_FILE or appending ::test_name.
`make test` only invokes pytest when the TEST_FILE path exists and otherwise prints a skip message instead of failing.

Lint, format, and type checks are separate gates from tests: `make lint` runs ruff check plus a ruff format --diff, `make format` fixes in place, and `make typecheck` runs basedpyright over agent/ and tests/.

The Playwright end-to-end suite is invoked from the root package.json via pnpm: test:e2e runs the browser suite, test:e2e:desktop runs the Electron/dcode-ACP flow, and test:e2e:install runs `playwright install --with-deps chromium` and must precede the first run.

The e2e suite drives the whole happy path end to end: a user mentions Open SWE in a mock Slack thread, the real agent runs via langgraph dev, implements the change in a local temp-dir sandbox, pushes a branch, opens a PR on a fake GitHub, and posts the PR link back to the same Slack thread.

In the e2e suite only the LLM and external SaaS HTTP boundaries are faked while all agent code runs for real: fake_llm.py is a scripted BaseChatModel, patches.py monkeypatches the boundaries, and fakes.py holds in-memory PR/Slack stores plus git seeding of a local bare remote that the mock UIs render as the single source of truth.

The e2e harness serves the real built ui/ dashboard app rather than a mock, so server rendering, the session gate, and /dashboard/api/* calls are exercised for real with a genuine signed session cookie.

Browser Playwright runs retain trace and video on failed attempts locally and on the first retry in CI, with screenshots on failure; E2E_ARTIFACTS=1 records trace and video for every attempt under test-results/ and playwright-report/.

The dashboard package runs its component and client unit suite with `vitest run`; the desktop package builds its main bundle and runs Node tests via `node --test test/*.test.cjs`, while root `pnpm test` delegates to Turbo's workspace test task.

The browser Playwright configuration runs serially against a real `langgraph dev` server, excludes the desktop spec, and uses a 90-second test timeout; the desktop configuration selects only desktop.spec.ts and raises its timeout to 180 seconds.

Dashboard thread API tests distinguish image and model validation, trusted run-start enrichment and Slack-to-web handoff, surfaced-thread read visibility, admin and automation posting authority, readable-thread pinning, existing-sandbox terminal and recovery-patch access, and lazy creation only for `run.start`.

The Electron e2e test resets shared harness state, clones the seeded local bare remote into an isolated temporary project, injects a harness-issued osw_session cookie, runs a local-agent request, and verifies both the local project edit and fake-GitHub PR fields.
Browser e2e builds and starts the real dashboard UI with its API bases directed to the harness; `E2E_FORCE_UI_BUILD=1` forces a rebuild after UI or port changes.

Sandbox-state tests require the backend proxy to remain BaseSandbox-compatible for capture offload, delegate or safely fall back from offload, share one concurrent reconnect, survive waiter cancellation, retry failed startup, and recover a sandbox ID from live thread metadata.
The Electron e2e spec explicitly traces its Electron context, attaches screenshots for unified and completed local-agent views, and removes temporary desktop state unless E2E_KEEP_TMP is set.

The e2e harness overlays the real agent API with fake GitHub/Slack endpoints, mock UIs, and control endpoints, and signs the simulated Slack Events API delivery before posting it to the real webhook route.

Beyond the basic Slack-to-PR flow, browser e2e tests cover Slack-to-web continuation, plan approval, environment authorization and propagation, Slack redelivery and busy-thread queueing, raw SSR authentication behavior, PR health presentation, and thread-tool changes reflected in the dashboard.

Dashboard CSRF tests require configured cookie-authenticated mutations to use an allowed Origin or Referer, reject malformed, null, missing, and prefix-bypass origins, permit the desktop origin, and reject non-JSON command payloads while reads skip the mutation origin check.

Agent assembly tests require the main agent to receive an initialized sandbox-backed composite backend, preserving deepagents context eviction and summarization support, and verify source-sensitive skills/tools plus middleware and parent-tool boundaries.

Dashboard activity tests refresh completed run status in listings and mark a finished thread viewed on read, but do not mark a running thread viewed; a surfaced Slack thread can be marked viewed by any authenticated user.
